0.content:
Adorno was Captain of the 5th Company, a veteran of Varka's campaigns, and in later years a semi-retired fixture of Dornman Port who handed out candy and rescued lost cats. Leading a rescue with blunt arrows, he freed the children Eroch's men had abducted, Lohen among them. The rescue earned him the title "Benevolent Knight", though he felt he never deserved it because he had failed to find the experiment site or ease Lohen's trauma. He guided Lohen from the Adventurers' Guild into the Knights. He recommended him for the Nod-Krai expedition on condition that Lohen reflect on what makes a virtuous knight and then inherit his title and captaincy.

In 6.6 Lohen brought the Traveler and Paimon to Dornman Port posing as "friends" to avoid a lecture; Adorno saw through it and was pleased he had companions at all. Adorno was attacked by one of the escaped Ursa-tainted monsters while protecting a child. As he lay dying, he told Lohen to let the title go if he did not want it and simply be true to himself.

1.content:
Theodore was kidnapped with Lohen as a child; Lohen remembers him as the "goof" who would not stop crying. He failed the knight exams, became a trainee medic of the 8th Company, and cared for the ageing Adorno. Recalling Eroch's lab from childhood, he restarted the Ursa experiments to make a life-prolonging serum. Lohen, who had read Theodore's health report on Adorno, cleaned up his escaped test subjects. He kept the secret and offered himself as a test subject because he wanted the power.

Lohen pushed the work on, captured monsters for testing and kept the Knights' investigation slow. He also warned Theodore never to use the serum on Adorno to save time. After a dose tested on Lohen failed and the Knights closed in, Lohen first planned to take Adorno away that night; then, at the lab, he told Theodore to quit, warning that in Adorno's state the serum would kill him: a gambler who keeps betting after losing only loses more. Theodore, who had taken Adorno to the lab, took the highest-concentration dose himself, and it failed. Lohen asked him whether he was really the person Adorno chose for the Benevolent name.

2.content:
Lohen came to the Knights already hunting Varka. Varka was the "living legend" who had driven Eroch to his death. As a recruit, Lohen ambushed him with arrows, smoke, traps and sedatives. Varka subdued him, confined him for a few days and told him to try again whenever he liked. Lohen came back with a bottle of Varka's favourite Dandelion Wine, heavily drugged; Varka shrugged off the dizziness by sheer will. The lesson stuck: real strength is the kind no trap or poison can shake.

Varka made him vice captain, took him on the expedition and says he only cares about fighting, not glory, and digs traps for him out of boredom. Varka also has a key to Lohen's room. Lohen jokes that Varka mainly leads people into battle and dumps the rest on Jean. In 6.6, Lohen asked for one night before confessing and swore on his honour as a knight. Varka granted it, noting it was the first such oath Lohen had ever made.

3.content:
Riding in his father's cargo wagon to deliver bows to Mondstadt, the young Lohen was taken by masked men in black robes. Skilled bandits had drawn his father away first, and the father, used to a quiet life, never fought back. In a cell with other crying children, Lohen hid an arrowhead in his sleeve and had nicked his ropes by the time Adorno's knights intercepted the transport. The plot belonged to Eroch, the Knights' Inspector, who was experimenting with one of Dottore's Segments on serum drawn from Ursa the Drake's flesh.

In the 6.6 lab, a memory-trap showed the Traveler a child's view from inside a transport box, with Fatui Oprichniki standing guard. A cold voice promised the new subjects they would rise above the "common clay" of the world. The lab's notes describe test subjects carrying under one percent of Ursa's power, used to spread dread and open the way for northern "allies". Lohen holds that Eroch hid his true colours so well that even his victims did not know who was responsible.

4.comment: Lohen: A Knight's Legacy and Ursa's flesh
4.content:
Lohen's story quest (6.6). Due to receive a title and the 5th Company captaincy at the expedition's award ceremony, Lohen took the Traveler to see Adorno. In a test of Sucrose's Simulation Training Bubble, a memory of Rerir set him off and he released an unfamiliar power. Ursa-tainted monsters were roaming near Dornman Port. Varka and Diluc learned that Theodore had restarted Eroch's experiments and that Lohen had joined him.

After an escaped monster mortally wounded Adorno, Lohen confessed in principle and asked for one night. He used it to chase Theodore to the hidden lab and stop him. While Varka, Diluc and the Traveler destroyed the last of Ursa's flesh, Lohen formally asked permission to attack and held back the caged monsters alone. He crushed a vial of serum to make himself the bait.

5.content:
On the Nod-Krai expedition Lohen barely visited the Favonius Keep, spending his time hunting the Wild Hunt in the wilds. With Varka he ambushed Rerir, the Rächer of Solnari, was badly beaten and spent days in camp. By the time he could stand, the Traveler and their allies had banished Rerir. Then he and part of the 5th Company were sent home, so he also missed the fight with Dottore.

He says he was slow, weak, powerless... mortal, the word Rerir used. He questions whether Rerir himself was not once mortal too. The memory haunts him and fuels his hunger for power. He still remembers the Wild Hunt fondly as endless live targets and says the expedition felt free.

6.content:
The Knights of Favonius' ranged company: crossbowmen and musketeers who split into squads to support other companies. Lohen calls it an ordinary ranged support team. Under Lohen its tactics changed: he charges ahead with a spear as both shield and bait, so his squads fire at will. The expedition came to know him as its "Frontline Suppression Officer". Mika says its members are always on standby for the thick of the action and that Lohen inspires them to follow his reckless tactics.

Lohen trains them with night-time surprise drills and live-target shooting, sometimes with himself holding the apple. He plans to balance glasses of Dandelion Wine on his marksmen's weighted weapons in a Fontaine-style endurance drill. Captain Adorno led it in a semi-retired capacity until his death; as of 7.1 the captaincy is vacant and Lohen remains vice captain. Gunther and Ursula are among his snipers.

7.content:
Mika, a surveyor close to Lohen's age, was flattered when the "notorious" senior praised his surveying device and asked about it. He then noticed that every area Lohen asked about went quiet within days, and that Lohen kept coming back with fresh cuts. He started leaving monster camps off the maps. Lohen says one look at Mika's face was enough to find them anyway.

During a campfire card trick, Mika began to suspect that Lohen had swapped his device for a fake, copied the data and returned it. The story never confirms it. In 6.2 Mika told the Traveler he admires Lohen's fighting spirit and thinks the two would hit it off. Lohen says Mika's nervous footsteps are unmistakable, even from the floor above.

8.comment: Lohen: The Traveler and the friendship fee
8.content:
Lohen met the Traveler at the Thousand Winds Temple in 6.4, while delivering Varka's letters. In 6.6 he paid them a 100,000-Mora "friendship fee", drawn from his unspent special-mission allowance, to pose as his friends before Adorno. He promised not to tell a single lie, and he didn't, though he narrated his methods "with some delicacy". By the end of the quest he trusted them to fight Ursa while he held the monsters, and Varka remarked that the fee had not been a complete waste after all.

He asked them to stay close in case something goes wrong: "Don't grow old on me." He calls them reliable and says they would make a good 5th Company captain. He tested Paimon in Wolvendom by asking how many letters he had given them, in case of Wild Hunt disguise. His birthday gift for a friend is a wrist crossbow that also fires backwards.

9.content: The Cardinal ran the expedition's administration and doubted Lohen at every turn. He asked Varka whether he was sure about this vice captain, took "special headache leave" after the spear drill, and sent the reminder "Focus on the mission. Don't complicate things" before the auction raid. When Lohen turned in a neat report on time, Seamus saw at once that Gunther or Ursula had written it. He still noted, grudgingly, that Lohen had checked it himself.

10.content: The Northern Intelligence Network's current head asked the expedition to destroy a smuggling auction operating in Nod-Krai, and the network doubted that strength alone would be enough. The plan called for quiet captures and surveillance. Lohen captured everyone on site, kept the fight away from Nasha Town and harmed no civilians. He also walked into the enemy's centre, picked a fight and displayed his spoils. Jean wrote to Varka that it was benevolent in outcome but hardly Favonius conduct.

11.comment: Lohen: Proof of Strength and the Formidable Foes Fieldbook
11.content: The Witch's Homework world quest built around Lohen (Of Various Foes, 6.6, permanent), staged by Nicole. Deciding that the best road to strength was to challenge the world's strongest, he began a Formidable Foes Fieldbook with Leifhelm and Slazhnev. A Dodoco-shaped messenger from Barbeloth told him he would face the dragon's might three times. He met Ineffa, then Durin, who fled when Lohen drew his weapon. At Stormterror's Lair he recited Nicole's script back to her, including its moral about Ursa, the angel who chose power. He said he disliked lectures, thanked "the production crew" and left. Nicole concluded that angels no longer guide humanity alone.

12.content: Diluc was the youngest captain in the Knights' history, and Lohen was set to break that record. Lohen notes that both of them were wronged by Eroch. Now that the scores are settled, he wonders whether Diluc might return, if not as the youngest captain then as the oldest knight. In 6.6, Diluc investigated monster remains wiped suspiciously "clean" and caught Lohen culling them. Lohen brushed him off and went after the one that got away.
